en: The Path of Discrimination 2: The Chapter on the Coupling 2.8. Discourse on the Supramundane What is the supramundane? It is the four paths, the four fruits of the ascetic life, and Nibbāna. This is called the supramundane. What is the mundane? It is the aggregates, the elements, the sense-bases, the faculties, the nutriments, the truths, the dependent origination, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path. This is called the mundane. In what way is it mundane? Because it is associated with the world, because it is bound to the world, because it is subject to the world, because it is conditioned by the world, because it is produced by the world, because it is generated by the world, because it is caused by the world, because it is rooted in the world, because it is supported by the world, because it is dependent upon the world, because it is contingent upon the world—therefore it is called mundane. In what way is it supramundane?

Because it is dissociated from the world, because it is unbound to the world, because it is not subject to the world, because it is not conditioned by the world, because it is not produced by the world, because it is not generated by the world, because it is not caused by the world, because it is not rooted in the world, because it is not supported by the world, because it is not dependent upon the world, because it is not contingent upon the world—therefore it is called supramundane. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the three realms; the supramundane is that which is not included within the three realms. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the five aggregates; the supramundane is that which is not included within the five aggregates. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the twelve bases; the supramundane is that which is not included within the twelve bases. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the eighteen elements; the supramundane is that which is not included within the eighteen elements. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the four nutriments; the supramundane is that which is not included within the four nutriments. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the four truths; the supramundane is that which is not included within the four truths. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within dependent origination; the supramundane is that which is not included within dependent origination. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is included within the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; the supramundane is that which is not included within these. Furthermore, the mundane is that which is accompanied by the suffering of birth, accompanied by the suffering of aging, accompanied by the suffering of sickness, accompanied by the suffering of death, accompanied by the suffering of sorrow, accompanied by the suffering of lamentation, accompanied by the suffering of despair, accompanied by the suffering of association with the unpleasant, accompanied by the suffering of separation from the pleasant, accompanied by the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks—therefore it is called mundane. In what way is it supramundane? Because it is dissociated from the suffering of birth, dissociated from the suffering of aging, dissociated from the suffering of sickness, dissociated from the suffering of death, dissociated from the suffering of sorrow, dissociated from the suffering of lamentation, dissociated from the suffering of despair, dissociated from the suffering of association with the unpleasant, dissociated from the suffering of separation from the pleasant, dissociated from the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks—therefore it is called supramundane. Which phenomena are supramundane? The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers,
the seven factors of enlightenment, the noble eightfold path, the four noble paths, the four fruits of recluseship, and Nibbāna.
These states are supramundane.
